title: Marr's levels and computational-level analysis
description: Computational theory, representation and algorithm, implementation; what a computational-level model of a cognitive capacity claims and does not claim.

title: Cognition as inductive inference
description: The problem of induction (Hume, Goodman), hypothesis spaces and inductive bias, identification in the limit and PAC sample complexity, and why learning without bias is impossible.

title: Bayesian inference as a model of cognition
description: Degrees of belief as probabilities; prior, likelihood, posterior, evidence; odds-form comparison of hypotheses; Beta–Bernoulli parameter learning and the posterior predictive; hierarchical priors.

title: Bayesian concept learning
description: Concepts as hypotheses about extensions; the size principle from strong sampling; posterior over hypotheses; hypothesis averaging for generalisation; graded versus rule-like generalisation (the number game).

title: Generative models of cognition
description: Knowledge as working models that generate observations; probabilistic programs; prediction, simulation and conditioning as ways of interrogating a generative model.

title: Graphical models, dependence and explaining away
description: Directed graphical models and their factorisation; causal versus statistical dependence; screening off and explaining away; intervention versus observation.

title: Models of categorisation
description: Prototype, exemplar and rational models of categorisation; parametric class models; mixture models and unknown numbers of categories; the limits of classification as a model of concepts.

title: Bayesian Occam's razor and model selection
description: Marginal likelihood penalises flexibility; Bayes factors; the size principle as a special case; model selection in cognition.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian models and learning to learn
description: Overhypotheses, shared priors across contexts, the blessing of abstraction, learning domain structures.

title: Models of causal learning
description: Causal structure and strength learning, causal theories as priors over causal models, blocking and backward blocking, intervention.

title: Inference algorithms and rational process models
description: Exact enumeration, rejection sampling, MCMC, particle filters and variational inference; the sampling hypothesis and resource-rational analysis as bridges from the computational to the algorithmic level.

title: Social cognition as inference about inference
description: Inferring goals, preferences, knowledge and beliefs of other agents by inverting generative models of planning and communication.

title: Model behaviour, measurement, evidence and causal claims
description: Keeping apart what a model predicts, what an experiment measured, what the correspondence between them shows and at which level, and what causal or mechanistic claim (if any) is licensed.

title: Bayesian data analysis of cognitive models
description: Scientists' models of people's models: parameter inference, posterior prediction and model checking, Bayes factors, and fitting cognitive models to behavioural data.
